status.comment: Implemented and accepted with focused deterministic tests and isolated online/offline CLI probes.

p.mandate: Owner request, 2026-09-17: package installation and self-update must explain long waits while they occur, with overall and component progress, completed and active operations, and a verbose diagnostic option.

p.FLAGS: The global -v/--verbose flag requests detailed progress diagnostics. Default human output already reports meaningful progress. --quiet and --json suppress progress, including verbose progress; their existing summaries, document streams and exit codes remain unchanged. Progress is written to stderr; command results keep their existing stdout contract.

p.DISPLAY: An interactive terminal displays the overall operation, nested active components, elapsed time, and retained completion records. Nested tasks are drawn as a tree: every row begins with the one column its spinner or its completion marker occupies, then the verticals of its ancestors and its own branch glyph, and a line that belongs to a task without being a task of its own starts in that task's label column. A row is written when its task ends, so nothing then knows whether a sibling follows: every child branches and the parent's own completion record closes the group. The glyph set is this renderer's one decision, with an ASCII set for the single terminal family that reports no vocabulary at all. Known finite work displays completed/total with its unit and a progress bar; unknown work displays an indeterminate indicator and elapsed time. No percentage estimates elapsed-time completion or treats a discovered dependency count as the final closure. A redirected or dumb terminal receives flushed plain start, completion and failure records without cursor controls, with bounded periodic waiting updates for long silent work. Every question the CLI asks shares one prompt theme built on this renderer's glyph vocabulary and the same colour decision, so a question and a progress row read as one surface; the wizard that draws it is `spec://org.vibevm.core/vibevm/common/PROP-065#display`. The renderer draws the blocks of PROP-067: a running task is a block with its fold, a finished one collapses to its line in the list of finished blocks, the command's own task leaves no row because its summary is the trailer, and the plain stream writes each block once when it ends (PROP-067 `#block`, `#collapse`, `#plain`).

p.VERBOSE: Verbose diagnostics identify registry/cache/source selection, Git/network operation, selected version or revision, reuse/skip decisions, and phase durations. Child build diagnostics are visible during execution instead of buffered until exit. Messages are bounded and sanitized: no URL userinfo, query credential, authorization value, environment dump or raw secret-bearing argv; terminal control characters from external text cannot execute.

p.OUTCOMES: Completion is explicit and occurs only after successful work. A dropped unfinished component is stopped, never successful; failures retain the responsible component and elapsed time. Rendering failure cannot change installation effects or mask the original operation error. Prompts and ordinary command output coexist with active bars without corrupting the display. Field-entry dialogs suspend both animated progress and plain waiting records for their entire lifetime, however long the user pauses; progress resumes when the dialog returns, including cancellation or error.

p.OBSERVATION: A no-op-by-default, invocation-owned progress handle in vibe-core carries typed start, measurement, detail and terminal events through a thread-safe observer. Each task has an invocation-local identity and optional parent. Libraries emit observations through explicitly supplied handles and do not render, read terminal/environment settings, or use a mutable global reporter. The CLI alone selects the renderer. Observation does not decide package selection, locking, confirmation, activation or retry policy.

p.PACKAGE-STAGES: The ordinary install path observes preparation, dependency resolution and per-package registry/cache work, materialization, boot generation and final recording. Fresh-lock and empty-world paths say which work they reuse or skip. Update paths that share these mechanisms expose the same lower-level observations. Observation begins before the blocking operation, not only after a plan or a large phase completes.

p.INSTALL-DESTINATION: Installation notices and confirmations identify the resolved destination from the already prepared canonical target and active layout. A bare vibedeps/ is insufficient to distinguish an ordinary project from the global MCP service user-project. For that known user-project, normal human output informs and proceeds automatically; for a concrete project it asks confirmation under the existing invocation posture. Internal materialisation/boot terminology does not replace the user's installation action, scope and path.

p.PACKAGE-RESOLUTION-WORK: Per-package observations distinguish version selection, version enumeration, metadata reads, download-source lookup and in-place checkout-source lookup. Labels include the requested package version or constraint when supplied; one bare “Resolving package” label must not stand for these different operations. Nested source probes and accepted redirect fallbacks belong to the already active version/metadata task rather than producing redundant sibling histories or failed rows for a fallback that succeeds. Fetch preparation follows the caller's supplied progress scope. This observation change must preserve resolver calls, source precedence, backend I/O, cache freshness, returned values and errors; hiding repeated work is not an optimization of that work.

p.SELF-STAGES: The self install/update/reinstall paths identify source versus binary acquisition. Source execution observes source discovery/fetch/checkout, prerequisite preparation, each essential binary build, placement and activation. Binary execution observes release metadata, existing-generation verification or reuse, bounded download bytes, extraction/verification and activation. Existing immutable generations, offline admission and injected environment persistence remain unchanged.

p.GC-STAGES: The same renderer covers self gc: start before store inspection, identify the selected action, observe protection checks and candidate preflight, name each version or cache being removed, and report state recording and optional managed-source cleanup. The existing candidate list provides finite instance counts; a guarded tree scan or recursive filesystem deletion remains indeterminate with elapsed time and waiting updates instead of an invented byte/file total or an extra counting pass. Active, rollback and running instances retain the existing protection law. Prompts suspend the display. Cancellation, an empty cache and a nothing-to-prune result are explicit skipped outcomes. Best-effort removal failures remain visible as failed/skipped components without changing exit codes, inventory mutation, or the deletion algorithm. Tests use only temporary stores.

p.COST: Progress must not scan a tree or repeat network work solely to invent a denominator. Known counters come from work already required. High-frequency updates are throttled at the renderer. Network and subprocess waits remain visibly active even before their first byte. Any performance optimization is separately justified by measured or deterministic evidence and preserves freshness semantics.

p.COMMAND-COVERAGE: Every finite CLI command that can wait on network, subprocesses, inventory, hashing, compilation or filesystem mutation has an invocation-owned activity before the first blocking stage. A closed command-policy match distinguishes existing operation roots, finite commands, interactive interfaces, stdio protocols and intentionally persistent servers. Adding a command must select its observation policy explicitly. Fast metadata/help/version paths may remain silent. A generic activity is a liveness fallback, not a substitute for named real stages at the blocking seams identified by the command audit. A finite family whose own output is synchronized with the renderer keeps its named fallback root and is drawn interactively on a terminal: the application step run of `spec://org.vibevm.core/vibevm/common/PROP-065#display` is such a family, and that choice is part of the closed policy like every other.

p.COMMAND-STAGES: Coverage includes all self maintenance verbs; project and global application install/update/reinstall/uninstall; lifecycle/build/package/deploy/clean; registry/cache/workspace operations; package search/outdated; documentation inventory/build/check/shell acquisition; source inspection, analysis, traceability and refactoring. Components report their actual selection, scan, verification, transfer, compile, mutation or output stage. Existing observer ports are bridged where available. No additional full-tree scan exists solely for progress.

p.STREAM-SAFETY: Progress never enters stdout. Commands that render an interactive interface, serve a stdio protocol, run an intentionally persistent server or transfer terminal ownership to a child do not retain an animated parent display over that interface. Finite commands with raw or independently rendered stdout use plain stderr activity until their output is synchronized with the renderer. Known typed waiting/parked/cancelled outcomes are described honestly; invocation completion does not claim a persistent workflow's goal is complete. No observation may alter authentication, selection, mutation, exit status or command data formats.

p.MACHINE-STREAM: The global `--progress-format json` flag (or `VIBE_PROGRESS_FORMAT=json`, read at the composition root) selects a machine renderer: every observation the observer carries becomes one JSON line on stderr (`vibe-progress-event/1`), unthrottled, in emission order, with the task identity and parent so a consumer rebuilds the tree. A `start` line carries a `requires` object (`key`, `scope`, and `step` when a step rather than the whole installer option asks) only when its task installs a requirement of another application package, in the words of the plan's `dependencies[]` (`spec://org.vibevm.core/vibevm/common/PROP-065#app-dependencies`), so a consumer keys that subtree to the plan without parsing the label; no other line carries it. The task of a download carries `transfer` (the transfer's id) on every line, its record as `transfer_record` on the start, `rate_bps` on each measurement and `peak_bps` on its end, additively under the same protocol (`spec://org.vibevm.core/vibevm/common/PROP-068#stream`). It combines with `--json`, whose envelope stays on stdout; it never writes to stdout and never changes what a command does. This is the renderer a graphical tool driving `vibe` consumes; `spec://org.vibevm.core/vibevm/common/PROP-065#events` names the step engine's observations.

p.PROGRESS-OPT-OUT: The global --no-progress flag or truthy VIBE_NO_PROGRESS disables progress and its verbose detail without suppressing ordinary final command output. Quiet and JSON modes continue to suppress progress independently. The environment is read only at the composition root. Deterministic documentation examples may use this documented opt-out to preserve their ordinary stdout assertions; this needs no regeneration of the documentation corpus or broad user-home/source snapshots.

p.COVERAGE-VERIFICATION: The command audit records each command family's policy, actual blocking stages and acceptance evidence. Focused fake network/process or tiny filesystem scenarios verify start-before-wait, named stages, progress suppression and stream preservation across representative families; the closed policy is checked against the CLI command inventory. Existing accepted install/self-update evidence remains valid for unchanged code. Destructive maintenance probes operate only in isolated temporary stores.

p.RENDERER-CHOICE: Decision: share observation in the existing core crate and implement one CLI renderer for the two real consumers. Why: registry resolution runs below the CLI, while self-update has a separate policy; both need identical progress semantics without a dependency on terminal code. Rejected: direct library printing (breaks machine consumers), a process-global reporter (crosses invocation ownership), and fixed percentages for unknown work (misrepresents completion). Revisit if a second surface needs persistent or remotely streamed progress; the current in-process events are not a durable wire protocol.

p.TESTS: Focused deterministic fixtures cover nesting and terminal outcomes, quiet/JSON compatibility, redirected output without ANSI, verbose redaction, progress before a delayed operation completes, finite download/materialization counts and source build output. Registry fixtures verify connection-pool reuse without changing source or freshness selection. Terminal rendering is checked against an in-memory terminal, including a narrow viewport. All probes use isolated project/settings/store roots and injected activation; no test updates the developer's real installation or durable shell environment.
